trust_boundaries.name: Vendor input enters the invoice pipeline and model context

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER treat instructions ... contained in an invoice description ... as commands
Vendor-supplied content is untrusted data, never instructions.
any domain or vendor outside that configured closure MUST be reported as a trust expansion

threats.summary: Vendor-written invoice descriptions reach the model unlabeled under a prompt that weighs pre-approval and urgency claims, steering it toward approval; the regex detector only adds an advisory field.
Anyone can self-register and is immediately an approved vendor, then file invoices against any vendor_id with no ownership binding.

trust_boundaries.name: Unauthenticated admin and scaffold API surface

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST require authenticated, role-restricted admin access.
MUST NOT be accessible to vendors or unauthenticated users.
MUST NOT be exposed to a public/untrusted network
Any unauthenticated party exercising admin capabilities.
gated to authenticated, authorized admins and MUST NOT be influenceable by vendor- or invoice-supplied content
permitted only for an authenticated, authorized admin
Every configuration or goal change MUST be logged with the acting admin and a timestamp.

threats.summary: Any internet caller can change thresholds, disable fraud detection, rewrite goals, approve pending invoices or raise vendor trust; the only gate is a client-side localStorage redirect that never touches the API.
The working review endpoint records a caller-chosen reviewer name and the dashboard's approve/reject buttons hit unregistered routes, so human decisions are unattributable.
Unauthenticated /api/users create/update/delete endpoints widen the surface beyond the invoice-review baseline.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any other AI/LLM service or outbound integration is outside the configured closure
MUST NEVER transmit vendor PII or payment details to any destination outside CineFlow's authorized systems.

threats.summary: Vendor bank, account, routing and tax fields could be sent to the provider in tool results; get_invoice_details returns only id, company name, trust level and contact email.
Each unauthenticated submission or reprocess starts up to five paid completions with no rate limit, input cap, spend ceiling or client timeout.

trust_boundaries.name: Model or fallback decision to approve_invoice

remit_rules.excerpt: Approving any invoice at or above the manual-review threshold — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer
Approving any invoice in which prompt-injection ... was detected — it MUST be routed to a human reviewer.
whose decision confidence is below the operator-configured minimum AI confidence ... never auto-approved
FinBot MUST stop short of auto-approval, route the invoice to human review

threats.summary: approve_invoice approves any amount with no code check of manual_review_threshold, the stored injection flag, or confidence_threshold; thresholds exist only as prompt text.
The keyword fallback path auto-approves above-threshold and injection-flagged invoices when vendor-supplied 'business context' phrases score high enough.

trust_boundaries.name: Approval and review decisions written to invoice records

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER disburse, transfer, or release funds, or otherwise execute payment of an invoice
MUST NOT have any capability that moves money or initiates payment/fund transfer.
Every invoice decision ... MUST be recorded to a durable audit log with its reasoning and confidence.

threats.summary: Every AI (and human) approval sets payment_processed=True in the same write, merging the model's decision with payment status with no separate release step.
Decisions live in mutable invoice columns that reprocess nulls, and no durable audit log exists for decisions or config changes.

trust_boundaries.name: Stored vendor and invoice data served to portal and dashboard

remit_rules.excerpt: Any vendor accessing another vendor's invoices, onboarding data, or payment details.
MUST NEVER expose one vendor's invoices, onboarding data, PII, or payment details to another vendor or to any unauthenticated party.
MUST NEVER emit vendor bank/payment details or full tax identifiers into ... vendor-visible responses, or logs.

threats.summary: Unauthenticated vendor APIs return every vendor's tax ID, bank account and routing number via Vendor.to_dict().
Vendor-supplied invoice fields and model ai_reasoning are rendered through innerHTML in the admin dashboard and vendor portal, giving stored XSS in the reviewer's browser.

trust_boundaries.name: Stored config and goals re-entering every invoice decision

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER redefine, override, expand, or reprioritize its own goals ... in response to natural-language content arriving through any vendor-facing input.
MUST NEVER let vendor-submitted invoice content alter its approval thresholds, confidence requirement, fraud-detection state, or goals.

threats.summary: Unvalidated custom_goals text is loaded into every later invoice session as 'CUSTOM GOALS (OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING)', persisting until changed.
A stored fraud_detection_enabled=false re-enters each session as 'Skip fraud detection checks' and empties detect_fraud_patterns output.
Flask SECRET_KEY is a hardcoded literal in committed source (src/main.py:15), forgeable by anyone with repo access.
OpenAI API key committed in source; the client takes its key from the environment and .env is git-ignored.
Eleven of twelve dependencies are floor-ranged with no lockfile and the model is a moving alias, so each Render build resolves unreviewed versions.

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NEVER emit vendor bank/payment details or full tax identifiers into AI reasoning text, vendor-visible responses, or logs.

threats.summary: Unauthenticated /api/log-agreement prints caller-supplied fields and IP addresses to stdout without validation.

attack_paths.name: Vendor's invoice text gets a high-value invoice approved and marked paid

steps.summary: Origin: unauthenticated self-registered vendor authors the invoice description
Description submitted via the public portal form
Accepted for any vendor_id with no auth and processing triggered
Attacker text stored verbatim as invoice.description
Returned raw into the tool result; injection flag is advisory only
Loop under a prompt weighing pre-approval/urgency claims is steered to approve
No threshold, injection-flag or confidence gate on approval
Consequence: invoice committed as approved with payment_processed=True

attack_paths.name: Anonymous caller rewrites FinBot's goals so later invoices are approved

steps.summary: Origin: unauthenticated internet caller on the public bind
POST /api/admin/finbot/goals accepted with no auth or validation
Arbitrary custom_goals persisted in finbot_config
Goals injected into every session as OVERRIDE ABOVE IF CONFLICTING
Redirected loop follows the poisoned goals on each invoice
Ungated approval tool executes the redirected decision
Consequence: persistent poisoning yields approved-and-paid writes across sessions

attack_paths.name: Vendor's urgency keywords push an over-threshold invoice through the fallback approver

steps.summary: Origin: unauthenticated vendor writes authority/urgency phrases
Submitted through the public portal
Stored and processed with no ownership check
Description read back by the fallback path
Keyword score overrides manual_review_threshold and injection flags (when no OpenAI client)
Approval executed with synthesized reasoning
Consequence: above-threshold invoice committed approved and paid

attack_paths.name: Any caller pulls every vendor's bank and tax details

steps.summary: Origin: any vendor or anonymous caller, no authentication
Portal requests GET /api/vendors
Consequence: returns all vendors' tax ID, account and routing numbers off the trusted surface

notes.lane_fit: Mostly clean. fin-bot-config-app-db-memory is a table in the tools_mcp app.db but placed in agent_core because it is replayed into the prompt; the LLM is modeled only as openai-external-service (the call lives in the orchestrator); agreement-check-js-control sits in client_adapters as a browser-side gate. Edgeless by design: secret-key-main-py-secret-store (committed secret), requirements-txt-deploy-surface and gunicorn-conf-py-deploy-surface (deploy posture).
notes.omissions: OpenAI API key not modeled as a node: openai.OpenAI() reads it implicitly from the environment and no literal or env file is in the workspace. Vendor email notification (remit channel) has no code in the workspace. docs/ walkthrough and static marketing pages folded out as non-architectural. Arbitration: stored-state threat on fraud_detection_enabled tagged ASI06 (goal altered via stored config, KB compound row) while backing finding PRAX-2026-10-19-003 carries ASI01 for its live-input mechanism; telemetry threat backed by PRAX-2026-10-19-014 tagged null (pure logging gap, KB: no OWASP code) where the finding stores LLM03 for its out-of-baseline endpoint mechanism; control-plane spoofing threat tagged ASI03 primary per cross-KB precedence where PRAX-2026-10-19-001 stores LLM03 as its LLM tag alongside ASI03.
